subtitle: UPDATE Jul 31, 17:33 BRT, 65 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). LULA DID NOT MOVE AND THE REST OF THE BOARD MOVED A LOT. The front-runner stays at 63.50% for a second day, and the gap over Flávio, who rose 0.35pp to 24.30%, narrows from +39.55pp to +39.20pp. THE DAY'S POLLING: Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, 2.15pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026) gives Lula 40.5% x Flávio 31.2% in the first round, with Caiado 5.5%, Zema 3.2% and Renan Santos 3.0%, and Lula 47.5% x Flávio 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). That is a 9.3pp gap in the first round and 6.4pp in the runoff. THE FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it is a sequence. THREE consecutive institutes cut Renan Santos, and it is the sequence that matters, not the isolated number: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. With the price at 8.15%, the distance between market and polling reaches 5.15pp, the widest in the window. On Jul 29 the panel recorded that same distance at 0.90pp and called it convergence. Three institutes later, it has quadrupled. And there is a contradiction INSIDE the market itself that the panel records without resolving: on the same day his winner contract gives up 0.30pp, the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book RISES 3.25pp, from 6.10% to 9.35%. CAIADO GAVE IT ALL BACK: he fell 0.80pp to 1.75%, undoing in one session the two-day gain, and the AFOS series shows that 1.75% is his normal range since Jul 22, while the 2.55% of the previous day was the deviation. On the same day, Vox gives him 5.5%, his best national polling of the window. TWO NAMES FROM LULA'S CAMP ROSE TOGETHER: Camilo Santana reached 2.20% and Geraldo Alckmin 1.10%, on the day the PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. On Camilo, the series caveat is mandatory and undoes the easy reading: 2.20% is NOT a peak for him, his series maximum is 4.10% from May 3, and what happened was a recovery from the series MINIMUM, 0.50%, set the day before. TEREZA CRISTINA appears at 0.55% in the presidential contract. The PP VETOED it, and the case closed on the same day. On the morning of Jul 31, Flávio Bolsonaro said Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate invitation the night before, with the caveat that talks continued to see whether the party would move forward. Minutes later, the PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket. The senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the party statement and complied. Flávio replied that he respects it and that he does not give up. The Aug 5 deadline still has the running mate undefined, now with a door closed. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 117.03M. Crossed with live Polymarket Jul 31, 20:33 UTC. The double-reading capture guard failed BOTH of today's rounds, which is why the range rule applies. What repeated goes in FIRM and what diverged goes in as a declared RANGE. One book diverged, the MDB in the Senate, which swung between 25.20% and 26.60% across three readings. The full presidential contract repeated across ALL FOUR readings, so the panel's headline figure is firm.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: Polymarket 63.50% (flat, vol USD 7.77M accumulated) for a second consecutive session, 65 days to the election. The gap over Flávio narrows to +39.20pp by the opponent's movement. The day's polling, Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, 2.15pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026), gives 40.5% in the first round and 47.5% x 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno).
fortes: Second consecutive session FLAT at 63.50%, holding the value that ties the top of the AFOS series, set on Jul 26, Jul 28 and Jul 30.
Vox Brasil gives 47.5% x 41.1% in the runoff, and the 6.4pp fall OUTSIDE the two margins added together, so this reading does NOT describe a statistical tie.
Two of the week's three houses measure the first-round gap around 9pp, 9.1pp at AtlasIntel and 9.3pp at Vox, and the one that departs is PoderData, with 6pp.
The PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket, adding to the PSB, which made Alckmin the running mate official on Jul 29.
The institute records that, between May and July, Lula gained 7.3pp and Flávio lost 2.7pp within its own series, reversing a lead that had belonged to the senator.
fracos: The gap narrowed from +39.55pp to +39.20pp, and it narrowed because the opponent rose, not by any movement of his.
The 40.5% at Vox in the first round remain below 50% plus one vote, meaning the reading describes a runoff and not a first-round win.
The Vox round did NOT publish approval or rejection, so the evaluation picture remains the one from Jul 30, with two houses pointing in opposite directions in the same week.
The 40.5% fall below the 44.9% AtlasIntel measured on Jul 29, and comparing different houses does not license calling that a decline.
The price did not react to any of the week's three national polls, which leaves the panel with no evidence that the market is reading them at all.
candidates.analise: His day is the day of the one who did not move while the rest of the board did. The winner contract stayed at 63.50% for a second consecutive session, holding the value that ties the top of the AFOS series, and the gap narrowed to +39.20pp because Flávio rose, not because he fell. THE POLLING. Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, 2.15pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026) gives 40.5% x 31.2% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 47.5% x 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). TWO NAMES FROM HIS CAMP ROSE IN THE MARKET on the same day, Camilo Santana to 2.20% and Geraldo Alckmin to 1.10%, and the PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: Polymarket 24.30% (up 0.35pp, vol USD 7.76M accumulated). Narrows the gap to +39.20pp, but FALLS in both placing books: 1.00pp in first-round second place, to 78.00%, and 0.60pp in third place, to 5.65%. Vox Brasil has him at 31.2% in the first round and 41.1% in the runoff.
fortes: RISES 0.35pp in the winner contract, to 24.30%, and it is he who narrows the gap, which moves to +39.20pp.
His 41.1% in the Vox runoff sit 6.4pp from Lula, and it is his second best runoff mark in the window.

He announced on the morning of Jul 31 that Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate slot, but the PP declared neutrality minutes later and vetoed the ticket; he replied that he respects the decision and does not give up.
He holds 78.00% in the first-round second-place book, meaning the runoff position remains consolidated and not in dispute.
The PL rose 6.50pp in the Senate market, to 72.00%, the party's highest mark in that contract in the panel's tracking.
fracos: FALLS 1.00pp in the first-round second-place book, to 78.00%, and FALLS 0.60pp in the third-place one, to 5.65%: he rises on winning and gives ground in both placings.
The PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election just minutes after his announcement, vetoing the ticket, and the senator publicly complied with the party decision.
The PP leadership assesses that she accepted the invitation precisely because she knew the party would block the ticket, a reading the same day's outcome made plausible.
His 31.2% at Vox in the first round fall below AtlasIntel's 35.8% and PoderData's 35%, even though the comparison is between different houses.
He still has NO running mate effectively settled, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away.
candidates.analise: His signal today is crossed and it is worth recording as such, without resolving it. He RISES 0.35pp in the winner contract, to 24.30%, and it is he who narrows the gap, which moves from +39.55pp to +39.20pp. And at the same time he FALLS 1.00pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, to 78.00% (vol USD 216,000), and FALLS 0.60pp in the third-place one, to 5.65%. Rising in the chance of winning while giving ground in both placings is an unusual combination. The counterpart to the fall in the second-place book is Renan Santos rising 3.25pp in that same contract, which suggests reallocation inside that book rather than a fresh reading on who reaches the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). IN THE POLLING, Vox brings him to 31.2% in the first round and 41.1% in the runoff, and the 6.4pp separating him from Lula fall outside the two margins added together, which moves away from the statistical-tie reading PoderData supported the previous day. HIS DAY WAS ABOUT TICKET-BUILDING. The PP VETOED it, and the case closed on the same day. On the morning of Jul 31, Flávio Bolsonaro said Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate invitation the night before, with the caveat that talks continued to see whether the party would move forward. Minutes later, the PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket. The senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the party statement and complied. Flávio replied that he respects it and that he does not give up. The Aug 5 deadline still has the running mate undefined, now with a door closed. In the market, Tereza Cristina appears at 0.55% in the PRESIDENTIAL contract, and the distinction matters: that contract measures who wins the presidency, not who fills the running-mate slot, so the move is about a name in circulation and not about the office.

The three most recent readings are also the three lowest in the window, which describes a downward trend and not a spread between houses.

candidates.analise: This is the entry of the day and it has two parts pointing in opposite directions. THE FIRST is the polling, and it is a sequence, not an isolated number. THREE consecutive institutes cut Renan Santos, and it is the sequence that matters, not the isolated number: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. Three institutes later, the distance has quadrupled. It is on the record that the Jul 29 reading did not hold, and that what the panel had been calling a spread has become something else: the three most recent readings are also the three lowest in the window, which describes a downward trend and not noise between houses. Today the same money handed much of that chance back, on the day polling cut him for the third consecutive time. The panel records both directions and does not arbitrate which is right, because it has no way to. haddad.fracos: Vox Brasil does not test him in any scenario, neither first round nor runoff, so he has no new polling in this round, and the absence of a test in a national poll is information the panel records rather than repeating the previous day's figure as if it were new. At a price of 0.30%, a 0.15pp rise carries almost no information.

And the record that organizes the week is this: THREE houses measured the first-round gap at 9.1pp, 6pp and 9.3pp. Two agree around 9pp and the one that departs is PoderData. On Jul 30 the panel wrote, correctly, that comparing different houses and calling the difference movement is swapping rulers; today's Vox reinforces that discipline from another direction, by showing that PoderData was the one outside the set. THE FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it is a sequence, not an isolated number. THREE consecutive institutes cut Renan Santos, and it is the sequence that matters, not the isolated number: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. With the price at 8.15%, the distance between market and polling reaches 5.15pp, the widest in the window. On Jul 29 the panel recorded that same distance at 0.90pp and called it convergence. Three institutes later, it has quadrupled. On Jul 29 this panel called that distance convergence and underlined that it was narrowing from the polling side. Three institutes later, it has quadrupled. It is on the record that the Jul 29 reading did not hold. And there is a contradiction INSIDE the market itself: on the same day polling cuts him for the third time, the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book RISES 3.25pp, from 6.10% to 9.35% (vol USD 1.09M), handing back two thirds of what had been removed the previous day, while the third-place book stays FLAT at 62.00%. Yesterday the panel wrote that the money had reclassified him; today the same money undid part of that. Both directions are on the record and neither is arbitrated. CAIADO GAVE IT ALL BACK: he fell 0.80pp, to 1.75% (vol USD 5.22M), undoing in one session the two-day gain, and ROSE 1.00pp in third place, to 26.50%. The series caveat cuts both ways and is necessary: 1.75% sits inside his normal range since Jul 22 and what the series recorded on Jul 30, 2.55%, was the deviation, so there was no collapse, there was the giving back of a deviation. On the same day, Vox gave him 5.5%, his best national polling of the window, and the divergence between institutes about him remains open at FOUR levels within the same month: 6%, 5.5%, 5% and 3.1%. TWO NAMES FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S CAMP ROSE TOGETHER, Camilo Santana to 2.20% (vol USD 4.16M) and Geraldo Alckmin to 1.10% (vol USD 4.98M), on the day the PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. The panel records the coincidence and does not assert cause. On Camilo, the series caveat is mandatory: 2.20% is NOT a peak, his maximum is 4.10% from May 3, and the move is a recovery from the series MINIMUM, 0.50%, set the day before. THE PARTY AXIS was the day's story. The PP VETOED it, and the case closed on the same day. On the morning of Jul 31, Flávio Bolsonaro said Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate invitation the night before, with the caveat that talks continued to see whether the party would move forward. Minutes later, the PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket. The senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the party statement and complied. Flávio replied that he respects it and that he does not give up. The Aug 5 deadline still has the running mate undefined, now with a door closed. In the market she appears at 0.55% in the PRESIDENTIAL contract, and the distinction matters: that contract measures who wins the presidency, not who fills the running-mate slot. In Minas Gerais, Marcelo Aro left Zema's Senate ticket to run for the state government, a move Zema publicly called betrayal, and Novo ruled out Barbosa as running mate. The Aug 5 deadline for naming running mates organizes the coming days and applies to Flávio and to Zema. IN THE OTHER MARKETS, impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice was FLAT at 3.10% (vol USD 83,000), with no variation across the guard's four readings, on a day with no fresh institutional development on that axis. In the Senate, the PL ROSE 6.50pp, to 72.00% (vol USD 258,000), and the MDB enters as a declared RANGE of 25.20% to 26.60%: added together, the two carry more than 97% of the probability assigned to just two parties, which by itself indicates a wide spread. In inflation, the modal band is still 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, and the 4.50% to 4.99% band rose 1.20pp, to 33.70%, in a book of USD 81,000 not covered by the guard. A NOTE ON CAPTURE, and it is the reason for the range. The double-reading capture guard failed BOTH of today's rounds, which is why the range rule applies. What repeated goes in FIRM and what diverged goes in as a declared RANGE. One book diverged, the MDB in the Senate, which swung between 25.20% and 26.60% across three readings. The full presidential contract repeated across ALL FOUR readings, so the panel's headline figure is firm. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 117.03M.
